adjudication_records.issue_text: Stored XSS: content imported with cook_method raw_html bypasses sanitization and is rendered raw in embed view and topic pages, allowing script execution from malicious feed content (nothing strips <script>, event handlers, or javascript: URLs; CGI.unescapeHTML even decodes entity-encoded markup)

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new `cook_method` enum with `:raw_html` and changes `Post#cook` to `return raw` when `cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, explicitly bypassing the normal cooking/rendering pipeline (which is where Discourse typically sanitizes HTML). `TopicEmbed.import` uses `PostCreator.new(..., raw: absolutize_urls(url, contents), skip_validations: true, cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html])`, so imported feed/remote content is stored and served as-is. In the embed UI it is rendered with `<%= raw post.cooked %>`, and because `post.cooked == post.raw` under `raw_html`, any `<script>`, `on*` handlers, or `javascript:` URLs present in RSS `i.content` (which is only `CGI.unescapeHTML(...scrub)` and not sanitized) will execute for readers. This is a verifiable stored XSS vector introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Attribute injection: url in the 'imported from' footer in topic_embed.rb is not HTML-escaped, so a URL containing a single quote can break out of the href attribute and inject arbitrary attributes/elements

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `TopicEmbed.import`, the footer HTML is built via string interpolation: ```rb contents << "... #{I18n.t('embed.imported_from', link: "#{url}")} ..." ``` `url` is only checked with `/^https?\:\/\//`, which does not prevent single quotes or other characters that can break out of the `href='...'` attribute. A value like `http://example.com' onclick='alert(1)` would produce an injected attribute in the generated `` tag. This content is then stored as raw HTML (`cook_method: :raw_html`), and later rendered with `raw post.cooked` in `app/views/embed/best.html.erb`, making this a verifiable XSS/HTML injection risk introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: PollFeed loop has no per-item error handling and the job has retry: false, so the first bad item (e.g. nil i.content causing NoMethodError, nil i.title causing NOT NULL violation, or nil embed.post) permanently blocks all subsequent feed items from being imported, with errors silently swallowed

topic_embeds rows are never cleaned up when their topic/post is deleted, causing EmbedController#best to raise on stale topic_id (permanent 500 with no recovery path) and TopicEmbed.import update path to call PostRevisor.new(nil)

adjudication.rationale:
The diff introduces `TopicEmbed` rows linking to `topic_id` and `post_id`, but there is no `dependent: :destroy` on the associations and no DB foreign keys with `ON DELETE CASCADE` in the migration—only a unique index on `embed_url`. Therefore if a Topic or Post is deleted, `topic_embeds` can become stale.

This can cause two concrete failures shown in the diff:
1) `EmbedController#best` uses `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` which `pluck`s `:topic_id` from `topic_embeds` without verifying the Topic still exists. If the topic was deleted, `TopicView.new(topic_id, ...)` is likely to raise (e.g., RecordNotFound), producing a 500 and never hitting the “enqueue retrieve + loading” recovery path.
2) `TopicEmbed.import` update path does `post = embed.post` and then (when content changed) calls `PostRevisor.new(post)`; if the post was deleted, `embed.post` is `nil`, so this becomes `PostRevisor.new(nil)` and will error.

These are direct, verifiable consequences of the code as written.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Remote fetches in import_remote (topic_embed.rb) and PollFeed use open-uri with no open_timeout/read_timeout and no response size limit, allowing slow or malicious hosts to hang Sidekiq workers and huge responses to exhaust memory

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, both `TopicEmbed.import_remote` and `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` perform remote HTTP fetches via Ruby's `open-uri` without specifying any `open_timeout`/`read_timeout` options or enforcing a maximum response size. Specifically: `Readability::Document.new(open(url).read, ...)` reads the entire response into memory, and `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` similarly streams/parses a remote response with no explicit limits. This can allow slow endpoints to tie up Sidekiq workers and very large responses to consume excessive memory.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The feed_key for caching feed modification state in poll_feed.rb is defined but never used, so the entire feed is re-downloaded and re-processed on every run

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, a `feed_key` method is defined (`"feed-modified:#{Digest::SHA1.hexdigest(...)}`) but it is never referenced anywhere in the job. The `poll_feed` method always does `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` and iterates all `rss.items` on every execution, with no conditional GET, no stored last-modified/etag, and no early exit based on cached state. While `TopicEmbed.import` may prevent duplicate topics/updates by URL/SHA1, the feed is still re-downloaded and fully processed each run. This matches the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: PollFeed iterates all feed items with no item cap, causing unbounded per-run work (SHA1 hashing, TopicEmbed lookups, topic creation) especially when also run inline from retrieve jobs

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, `poll_feed` does `rss.items.each` with no limiting, pagination, or early exit, and for each item calls `TopicEmbed.import`, which computes a SHA1 and performs DB lookups/creates/updates. Additionally, `lib/topic_retriever.rb` calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` inline during `perform_retrieve` whenever `feed_polling_enabled?` is true, meaning a single embed retrieval can trigger processing the entire feed. This creates unbounded per-run work proportional to feed size.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a `:raw_html` cook method in `Post` where `cook` immediately returns `raw` (`return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`), bypassing the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline. `TopicEmbed.import` creates posts with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and `raw` set to `absolutize_urls(url, contents)`, which only rewrites relative `href`/`src` values via Nokogiri and does not sanitize tags/attributes. `Jobs::PollFeed` sources `content` from an external feed using only `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` (no sanitization) before passing it into `TopicEmbed.import`. Finally, the embed UI renders the content with `<%= raw post.cooked %>` in `app/views/embed/best.html.erb`, and for `:raw_html` posts `post.cooked == post.raw`, so any injected `<script>` or event-handler attributes from third-party content would execute under the Discourse origin. This is a real stored XSS vector introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: RSS feed path (Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed -> TopicEmbed.import) passes raw feed content into raw_html cook path with no filtering, allowing script/iframe/onerror attributes in stored cooked content (stored XSS)

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed`, the code takes feed-provided HTML (`i.content`), only does `CGI.unescapeHTML(...scrub)`, and passes it to `TopicEmbed.import`. `TopicEmbed.import` creates a post with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and sets `raw` to `absolutize_urls(url, contents)` (which only rewrites relative `href`/`src` and does not sanitize). The diff also changes `Post#cook` to `return raw` when `cook_method == :raw_html`, explicitly skipping the normal cooking/rendering pipeline (where sanitization would typically occur). Finally, the embed view renders `raw post.cooked`, so any `<script>`, `<iframe>`, or event-handler attributes from the feed can be stored and executed (stored XSS).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Even in the whitelisted path, the readability tag whitelist allows javascript: hrefs since attributes %w[href src] are permitted without scheme validation

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `TopicEmbed.import_remote`, the code constructs `Readability::Document` with `tags: ... a img` and `attributes: %w[href src]` and then imports `doc.content` via `TopicEmbed.import`. That imported content is stored as a post with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, and `Post#cook` returns `raw` directly (bypassing the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline). The embed view renders it with `<%= raw post.cooked %>`. There is no scheme/URL validation for `href`/`src` anywhere in this path (only relative URLs starting with `/` are rewritten). Therefore `javascript:` (or other dangerous schemes) in `href` can survive the “whitelist” and be rendered, which is a real XSS risk introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: topic_embed.rb:14 interpolates feed-controlled url directly into unescaped href='#{url}', allowing single-quote breakout into arbitrary HTML
force: true added to already-shipped migration 20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb, causing silent drop of the top_topics table and its data on any re-run

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes an existing migration `20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb` from `create_table :top_topics do |t|` to `create_table :top_topics, force: true do |t|`. In Rails, `force: true` causes the table to be dropped and recreated if it already exists. If this migration is ever re-run (e.g., during `db:migrate:reset`, rebuilding an environment by replaying migrations, or other rerun scenarios), it would silently drop `top_topics` and lose its data instead of failing loudly, which is a real data-loss risk introduced by this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The new create_topic_embeds migration also uses force: true, which would silently drop the table on any partial re-run

adjudication.rationale: The new migration `db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb` explicitly does `create_table :topic_embeds, force: true`. In Rails, `force: true` will drop an existing table of the same name before creating it (typically via `DROP TABLE IF EXISTS`), which can cause silent data loss if the migration is run when the table already exists (e.g., schema drift / partial re-run).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Disqus import CLI drops the --category method_option with no replacement, breaking existing callers passing -c

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes `method_option :category, aliases: '-c'` from `lib/tasks/disqus.thor` and deletes the associated `category_id` lookup and passing `category: category_id` into `PostCreator`. The new implementation calls `TopicEmbed.import_remote(...)` and provides no replacement for specifying a category. As a result, any existing scripts/callers invoking the Thor task with `--category`/`-c` will now fail with an unknown option or lose the ability to target a category.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Rewriting Disqus import from PostCreator to TopicEmbed.import_remote silently discards created_at, so imported posts get import-time timestamps with no way to preserve the original

adjudication.rationale: In `lib/tasks/disqus.thor`, the initial topic/post creation previously used `PostCreator.new(... created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at]) ...)`, explicitly preserving the thread’s original timestamp. The diff replaces that with `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])`. `TopicEmbed.import_remote` only uses `opts[:title]` and then calls `TopicEmbed.import`, which constructs `PostCreator.new(... skip_validations: true, cook_method: ...)` without passing `created_at`. Therefore the created topic/post will get the current time as `created_at`, and this code path provides no way to pass/preserve the original `t[:created_at]`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: PollFeed job crashes on nil i.content (feed items lacking content/description), and sidekiq retry: false means one malformed item kills the entire hourly poll and skips subsequent items, with no rescue or logging
SimpleRSS.parse open(...) can raise on network/parse errors with no error handling in the poll feed job

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, `rss = SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` performs a network fetch and then parses the response without any `begin/rescue` handling. Both `open(...)` (network/timeouts/HTTP errors) and `SimpleRSS.parse(...)` (malformed feed) can raise exceptions, which would cause the scheduled job to error out (and it is configured with `sidekiq_options retry: false`, so failures won’t be retried). This lack of error handling is a concrete defect in the added code path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: embed.js postMessage origin check uses substring containment (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin)) instead of exact origin equality, and never checks e.source is the iframe's contentWindow
raw_html early return in Post#cook happens before Plugin::Filter.apply(:after_post_cook, ...), silently skipping the plugin filter contract for raw_html posts

adjudication.rationale: In app/models/post.rb, Post#cook now returns `raw` immediately when `cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`. This bypasses the existing call to `Plugin::Filter.apply(:after_post_cook, self, ...)`, meaning plugins relying on the `:after_post_cook` hook will not run for these raw_html posts. That is a behavior change introduced by the diff and is directly verifiable from the new early return.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Non-atomic setnx/expire throttle in TopicRetriever can leave a Redis key with no TTL if the process dies between calls, permanently blocking the embed URL for non-staff users

adjudication.rationale: In lib/topic_retriever.rb#retrieved_recently?, throttling is implemented as two separate Redis calls: `$redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` followed by `$redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)`. If the process crashes or is terminated after `setnx` succeeds but before `expire` executes, the key will be created without a TTL. Since subsequent calls use `setnx` (which will then return false), the code will always treat it as "retrieved recently" and return true, effectively permanently throttling that embed URL for non-`no_throttle` users. This failure mode is directly implied by the non-atomic setnx/expire sequence in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Embed view crashes when post author is deleted because post.user is nil, raising 500 in the /embed/best iframe (post.user.small_avatar_url)

adjudication.rationale: In the new `app/views/embed/best.html.erb`, the template calls `post.user.small_avatar_url` and `post.user.username` without a nil-guard, so it *would* raise if `post.user` were nil. However, the diff does not show any change that would allow `Post#user` to be missing (no association/schema change, and imported posts are created with a concrete `user` passed to `PostCreator`). Whether “deleted author” results in `post.user == nil` depends on existing Discourse user-deletion semantics not shown here (many apps keep a placeholder/anonymized user rather than removing the row). Thus the finding relies on an unproven assumption about behavior outside the diff and is not verifiably a real defect introduced here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: TopicEmbed.import update path calls PostRevisor.new(post) with no nil check on embed.post, so a destroyed post crashes Jobs::RetrieveTopic

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the update path does `post = embed.post` and then unconditionally instantiates `PostRevisor.new(post)` if the content hash changed. Since `topic_embeds.post_id` is not a foreign key and `belongs_to :post` doesn’t enforce presence at runtime, `embed.post` can be `nil` if the referenced Post row was deleted, causing an exception. However, the finding’s stated impact on `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` is not accurate because `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve` returns early when a `TopicEmbed` already exists for the URL, so it wouldn’t call `import` in that scenario.

adjudication_records.issue_text: <%- end if %> in embed/best.html.erb only compiles by accident because the next ERB statement is swallowed as the if condition; any edit to the following line causes a SyntaxError and 500s every /embed/best response
matched_golden_ids: The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both point out the same underlying ERB/Ruby syntax bug: using `<%- end if %>` to close an `if` block is invalid and can lead to a SyntaxError at render; it should be just `end` to close the block.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Anonymous /embed/best enqueues a RetrieveTopic Sidekiq job on every cache-miss for an unknown embed_url (user_id: nil), creating an unauthenticated job-enqueue/DoS vector

adjudication.rationale: In EmbedController#best, when TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url) returns nil, the action unconditionally enqueues Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, user_id: current_user.try(:id), embed_url: embed_url) and renders 'loading'. There is no authentication requirement in the controller, so current_user can be nil, producing user_id: nil. The only gate is ensure_embeddable, which checks SiteSetting.embeddable_host and compares it to request.referer host; a client can supply a Referer header matching the configured host. Although the RetrieveTopic job/TopicRetriever later throttles per-embed_url via Redis, the enqueue itself still occurs and can be amplified by varying embed_url values (even for invalid-host embed_url, the job is still enqueued before being discarded), creating an unauthenticated job-enqueue/DoS vector on cache-misses.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Stored XSS: remote HTML scraped via TopicEmbed.import_remote (Readability tag whitelist doesn't sanitize attribute payloads like javascript: hrefs) is persisted and rendered raw with no sanitization on write or render path (Post#cook raw_html + embed view raw post.cooked)

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a `raw_html` cook mode that makes `Post#cook` return `raw` directly (`return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`), bypassing Discourse’s normal cooking/sanitization pipeline. `TopicEmbed.import_remote` fetches remote HTML (`open(url).read`) and uses `Readability::Document` with a tag/attribute allowlist, but nothing in this diff sanitizes attribute values/protocols (e.g., `href="javascript:..."`) or strips event handlers if they slip through. The imported HTML is persisted as post `raw` (via `PostCreator` with `cook_method: :raw_html`) and then rendered as HTML in the embed view via `<%= raw post.cooked %>`, which will output attacker-controlled markup if the source page/feed is malicious. `absolutize_urls` only rewrites relative `/...` URLs and does not prevent `javascript:` or similar payloads.

adjudication_records.issue_text: HTML injection via embed_url in the 'imported from' footer in TopicEmbed.rb — url is interpolated directly into a single-quoted href with no escaping, allowing attribute breakout and stored XSS reachable from public /embed/best endpoint

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `TopicEmbed.import`, `url` is interpolated directly into HTML: `"#{url}"` and appended to `contents`, which is then saved into a post with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` (so `Post#cook` returns `raw` unchanged). The only validation on `url` is `return unless url =~ /^https?\:\/\//`, which still allows quotes and other characters (e.g., `http://example.com' onmouseover='alert(1)`), enabling attribute-breakout and stored XSS. The embedded view (`app/views/embed/best.html.erb`) renders `raw post.cooked`, making the payload executable when viewed via `/embed/best` (given the referer/host check passes).

adjudication_records.issue_text: No error handling or timeouts on any network fetch (PollFeed, import_remote open(url).read, TopicRetriever fetch_http) — network errors crash the poll with no log-and-continue, and the 60-second Redis throttle key is set before the fetch so transient failures with retry: false never actually retry

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces multiple network fetches using `open-uri` without any timeout or rescue handling: `Jobs::PollFeed` does `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` and `TopicEmbed.import_remote` does `open(url).read`, and `TopicRetriever#fetch_http` calls `TopicEmbed.import_remote` without rescuing exceptions. Any network error (timeout, DNS, 500, etc.) would raise and crash the job/request path. Additionally, `TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently?` sets the Redis throttle key (`setnx` + `expire`) before `perform_retrieve` runs; if `perform_retrieve`/HTTP fetch then fails, subsequent calls within 60 seconds will be throttled and won’t retry. For the scheduled poller, `sidekiq_options retry: false` means a transient fetch failure will not be retried by Sidekiq either.

adjudication_records.issue_text: On-demand embed request (RetrieveTopic job) runs a full synchronous feed poll via Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({}) inline, bypassing Sidekiq, causing heavy long-running work per page-load and racing the hourly scheduled poll

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve`, when `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` is true it directly calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` (see `lib/topic_retriever.rb`) instead of enqueueing a Sidekiq job. Since `EmbedController#best` enqueues `:retrieve_topic` when no embed exists, each on-demand embed retrieval can synchronously run a full feed fetch/parse inside the `RetrieveTopic` Sidekiq job, potentially making that job long-running and duplicating/racing with the separately scheduled hourly `Jobs::PollFeed`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Infinite reload/retry loop with no terminal failure state — if retrieval permanently fails the loading page reloads every 30 seconds indefinitely, each reload enqueues another RetrieveTopic job, and the throttle is bypassed entirely for staff (no_throttle: user.staff?) causing unbounded remote fetches

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a loading view (`app/views/embed/loading.html.erb`) that unconditionally `document.location.reload()` every 30 seconds with no stop/terminal error state. In `EmbedController#best`, when no topic is found it enqueues `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)` and renders this loading page. Therefore, if retrieval never succeeds, the page will reload forever and each reload will enqueue another `RetrieveTopic` job. Additionally, `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` passes `no_throttle: user.try(:staff?)` into `TopicRetriever`; in `TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently?`, `@opts[:no_throttle]` disables the Redis 60-second throttle entirely, so for staff users each enqueued job can trigger `fetch_http` and `open(url)` repeatedly, leading to unbounded remote fetch attempts when failures persist.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Referer-only guard with no rate limiting on the /embed/best enqueuing endpoint — forged Referer plus arbitrary embed_url enables request amplification against the job queue and embedded host; throttle is per-URL so varying the path bypasses it

adjudication.rationale: The new `/embed/best` endpoint enqueues `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ..., embed_url: embed_url)` whenever `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` returns nil, and there is no controller-side rate limiting or other robust auth. The only access control added is `ensure_embeddable`, which trusts `request.referer` (`URI(request.referer || '').host == SiteSetting.embeddable_host`), but the Referer header is client-controlled and can be forged in direct requests. Once enqueued, the job runs `TopicRetriever#retrieve`, whose throttling key is `retrieved:#{@embed_url}` (full URL); an attacker can vary the path/query of `embed_url` on the allowed host to bypass the 60s throttle and cause many jobs and outbound fetches (`open(url).read` via `TopicEmbed.import_remote`). This supports the finding’s amplification concern (job queue + repeated remote fetches) and the bypass via varying URLs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: i.content.scrub in PollFeed crashes the whole poll if a feed item lacks content (nil.scrub raises NoMethodError), aborting the poll and blocking later items — combined with retry: false one malformed item permanently blocks all feed imports
matched_golden_ids: Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both point out that calling `i.content.scrub` can raise an exception when `i.content` is nil because some feeds omit the `content` field. The candidate emphasizes the broader impact (poll aborts / blocks imports) but it’s the same underlying nil-content crash issue the golden comment describes (and implies the need for a fallback).

adjudication_records.issue_text: force: true added to create_table in already-shipped migrations (create_top_topics.rb and create_topic_embeds.rb) silently drops the table and its data if it already exists or the migration re-runs

Referer validation in EmbedController is brittle with no fallback when Referer is absent or stripped (HTTPS-to-HTTP, referrer policy, host casing mismatch like EvilTrout.com vs eviltrout.com) — embedding breaks entirely with no graceful error state

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable`, access is denied unless `URI(request.referer || '').host == SiteSetting.embeddable_host`. If the Referer header is missing/stripped, `URI('')` yields `host=nil`, so the comparison fails and it raises `Discourse::InvalidAccess` (no fallback). This behavior is also sensitive to exact string equality: `SiteSetting.embeddable_host` is not normalized (e.g., could be set to `EvilTrout.com`), so even if `URI(...).host` is normalized/lowercased, the direct `!=` check can incorrectly reject valid embeds. The diff therefore introduces brittle referer-based validation that can break embedding entirely when Referer is absent or mismatched in casing.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Origin check in embed.js uses substring matching (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin)) instead of exact origin parsing/comparison, breaking resize on scheme/port mismatches and misconfigured discourseUrl

Test at spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:44-48 asserts TopicRetriever is instantiated and retrieve is called, but EmbedController#best enqueues a background job and never instantiates TopicRetriever directly, so the expectation cannot be satisfied by the real code (test verifies mocks, not the job enqueue/argument passing/fallback render behavior)

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `EmbedController#best` does **not** instantiate `TopicRetriever` or call `retrieve`. When `topic_id` is nil it does `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, user_id: ..., embed_url: embed_url)` and `render 'loading'`. Therefore the spec in `spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb` that mocks `TopicRetriever.new` and expects `retriever.retrieve` (lines 44-48 per finding) cannot be satisfied by the actual controller code and would fail; it should instead assert the job enqueue / arguments / rendered template.

adjudication_records.issue_text: View rendering path (embed/best.html.erb, loading.html.erb, layouts/embed.html.erb) is completely untested because TopicView is stubbed in the 'creates a topic view' test, leaving untested raw HTML rendering (stored-XSS surface with raw post.cooked), the postMessage height script with request.referer interpolation into JS, and nil-safety when @topic_view.posts is empty
matched_golden_ids: An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate explicitly calls out the "postMessage height script" having `request.referer` interpolated into JavaScript, which aligns with the golden issue of unescaped referer leading to XSS. Although it mentions additional concerns (untested rendering, raw HTML, nil-safety), it includes the same underlying vulnerability.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Post#cook returning raw verbatim and skipping Plugin::Filter.apply(:after_post_cook) for raw_html posts has no direct test coverage — no spec verifies plugin filters are bypassed, the markdown pipeline (sanitization, onebox) is skipped, or how cook_method interacts with PostRevisor on re-import

adjudication.rationale: The diff does add a new code path in `Post#cook` that returns `raw` when `cook_method == :raw_html`, thereby skipping `post_analyzer.cook` and `Plugin::Filter.apply(:after_post_cook, ...)`. However, the proposed finding is primarily about lack of test coverage rather than a concrete defect. There *is* spec coverage that indirectly confirms the pipeline is skipped: `spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb` asserts `post.cooked == post.raw` when `cook_method` is `:raw_html`. There is no explicit spec asserting `Plugin::Filter` is bypassed or that onebox/sanitization are skipped, but “missing explicit tests” is not itself a verifiable bug/security/correctness problem in the diff, and part of the claim (“no spec verifies the markdown pipeline is skipped”) is contradicted by the existing `cooked == raw` assertion. The re-import path is also exercised (update spec), even if it doesn’t assert detailed `cook_method`/filter interactions.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The only positive poll test (spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb:33-38) mocks away all real feed logic: SimpleRSS.parse/open-uri fetching, the i.link/i.id fallback, CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub) which will raise NoMethodError on items without content, and the TopicEmbed.import delegation are all untested

adjudication.rationale: In spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb the only “positive” test (“delegates to poll_feed”) stubs the SiteSetting guards and only asserts `poller.expects(:poll_feed).once`, so it never executes `poll_feed` and therefore does not exercise any of the newly-added feed logic in app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb (the `open(...)` fetch, `SimpleRSS.parse`, the `i.link`/`i.id` fallback, `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`, or the call to `TopicEmbed.import`). This is directly verifiable from the diff: there are no tests that call `poll_feed` or assert behavior of those internals.

adjudication_records.issue_text: New job app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb has zero spec coverage — untested behavior includes Discourse::InvalidParameters on missing embed_url, user lookup with stale/absent user_id, and the no_throttle: user.try(:staff?) security-relevant throttle bypass

adjudication.rationale: The diff does add a new job `app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb`, and there is no corresponding spec file covering it (existing new specs are for `TopicRetriever`, `EmbedController`, `PollFeed`, and `TopicEmbed`). However, “zero spec coverage” is not itself a verifiable defect/bug/security issue in the code; it’s a process/quality concern. The mentioned behaviors (raising `Discourse::InvalidParameters` when `embed_url` is missing, handling missing `user_id`, and passing `no_throttle: user.try(:staff?)`) are indeed present, but the finding only asserts they are untested—not that they are incorrect or exploitable based on the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Redis throttle logic in topic_retriever is never tested because retrieved_recently? is stubbed in both directions — the $redis.setnx/expire 60-second throttle is unverified, including the failure mode where setnx succeeds but expire never runs (permanent throttle key), and invalid_host?'s URI::InvalidURIError rescue path is not actually tested

adjudication.rationale: The new `TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently?` method contains the actual Redis throttle logic (`$redis.setnx` + `$redis.expire(…, 60)`), but in `spec/components/topic_retriever_spec.rb` both “calls perform_retrieve” and “doesn't call perform_retrieve” cases stub `retrieved_recently?` to `false`/`true`, so the `$redis` behavior is never exercised or asserted. Also, the spec case `TopicRetriever.new("not a url")` likely results in `URI("not a url")` producing a URI object with `host == nil` rather than raising `URI::InvalidURIError`, meaning the `rescue URI::InvalidURIError` path in `invalid_host?` is not actually covered by the test as written.

adjudication_records.issue_text: TopicEmbed.import_remote (readability extraction used by the retriever and disqus thor task) has no test at all, and absolutize_urls only has happy-path coverage — missing tests for protocol-relative URLs (//cdn.example.com/x matches start_with?('/') but produces broken http://host//cdn... href), non-standard ports, and https URLs

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `TopicEmbed.import_remote` (used by `TopicRetriever#fetch_http` and the Disqus thor task), but the only new model spec (`spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb`) tests `.import` and does not exercise `.import_remote` at all. Also, `.absolutize_urls` rewrites any `href`/`src` that `start_with?('/')`; this will incorrectly rewrite protocol-relative URLs like `//cdn.example.com/x` as a path under the embed host (e.g. `http://eviltrout.com/cdn.example.com/x`), and there are no tests covering that case (nor separate cases for non-standard ports / https).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Referer-mismatch security check in ensure_embeddable has no test: no test for a referer from a different host than embeddable_host, no test that prefix-matching tricks like http://eviltrout.com.evil.com/ are rejected, and no test that the URI::InvalidURIError rescue path returns an error rather than 500ing on a garbage referer

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable`, which rejects requests when `URI(request.referer).host != SiteSetting.embeddable_host` and rescues `URI::InvalidURIError` to raise `Discourse::InvalidAccess`. The added controller spec covers: missing `embed_url`, missing `embeddable_host`, and missing referer, plus a success case with a valid referer. It does *not* include a test where the referer host differs from `embeddable_host`, nor a test for the `URI::InvalidURIError` rescue path (e.g., a garbage referer). The finding’s point about “prefix-matching tricks” is a bit mismatched because the implementation uses strict host equality (not prefix matching), but it’s still true there is no test asserting such a case is rejected.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Update path assertions in topic_embed_spec are too weak: the test only checks cooked =~ /new contents/, doesn't assert cook_method == raw_html and cooked == raw still hold after PostRevisor (i.e., the revisor doesn't re-run the markdown pipeline and mangle raw HTML), and there's no idempotency test for importing unchanged content (the sha1-equality short circuit hit on every hourly PollFeed run)

adjudication.rationale: The finding is about test strength/coverage rather than a verifiable defect introduced by the diff. While `topic_embed_spec`’s update assertion is indeed minimal (`cooked =~ /new contents/`), the diff does not show `PostRevisor` changing `cook_method` or forcing the markdown pipeline to run; `Post#cook` explicitly returns `raw` when `cook_method` is `:raw_html`, and imported posts set `cook_method` via `PostCreator`. Also, idempotency for unchanged content is already implemented in `TopicEmbed.import` via the `content_sha1 != embed.content_sha1` guard; the absence of an explicit spec for it is not a correctness bug in the code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb:2 has a copy-paste error: require_dependency 'jobs/regular/process_post' instead of the poll feed job, documenting the wrong dependency; similarly topic_retriever_spec.rb requires 'topic_retriever' as a dependency while retrieve_topic.rb relies on auto-requiring it

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb` contains `require_dependency 'jobs/regular/process_post'`, which is unrelated to the subject under test (`Jobs::PollFeed`, added in `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`). This looks like a copy/paste mistake and can lead to misleading or brittle spec loading (it doesn’t explicitly load the job it’s testing). However, the second claim is not supported: `app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb` *does* explicitly `require_dependency 'topic_retriever'`, so it is not “relying on auto-requiring.”

adjudication_records.issue_text: Assertions in spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:34-38 are hidden in an after block, so response.should be_success and header assertions run even when the example body fails, producing confusing double-failure output

adjudication.rationale: In spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb within the `context "success"`, lines 34-38 place `response.should be_success` and the `X-Frame-Options` header assertion inside an `after` block. RSpec `after` hooks run even when the example body fails, so if an example fails earlier (e.g., an unmet expectation like `TopicRetriever.expects(:new)`), the `after` hook will still execute and can add additional assertion failures (or even raise due to missing response state), producing confusing multi-failure output. This is a verifiable issue introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Raw-HTML cook path in app/models/post.rb:131-133 skips the Plugin::Filter.apply(:after_post_cook) pipeline entirely, silently breaking plugins that hook the cooking pipeline

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `Post#cook` to early-return `raw` when `cook_method` is `:raw_html`, which does bypass `Plugin::Filter.apply(:after_post_cook, ...)`. However, this bypass is explicitly intentional per the added comment (“skip the rendering pipeline”) and only applies to posts opting into `raw_html` (new feature for RSS/embed importing). The claim that this is a *bug* because it “silently breaks plugins” is speculative: the diff does not establish a requirement that `:after_post_cook` must always run even when cooking is intentionally skipped, nor does it show any plugin contract being violated in-core.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Raw-HTML cook path returns unsanitized external content as cooked HTML, which embed/best.html.erb renders with raw post.cooked, enabling XSS from the embedded host's content

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly introduces a `:raw_html` cook method (`Post.cook_methods`) and changes `Post#cook` to `return raw` when `cook_method == :raw_html`, bypassing the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline (`post_analyzer.cook`). `TopicEmbed.import` creates posts with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` from externally-sourced HTML (`SimpleRSS` feed content via `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` and `Readability::Document#content`). The embed view renders this HTML using `<%= raw post.cooked %>` in `app/views/embed/best.html.erb`, so any unsafe HTML in the imported content will be rendered as-is. There is no sanitization step shown in the diff for the raw-html path, making XSS from imported/embedded content a real, verifiable risk introduced by these changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: TopicRetriever#fetch_http crashes with NoMethodError on nil when SiteSetting.embed_by_username is blank but embeddable_host is set (lib/topic_retriever.rb:47)

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `lib/topic_retriever.rb`, `fetch_http` does `SiteSetting.embed_by_username.downcase` without checking presence. If `embeddable_host` is set/matching (so `invalid_host?` is false) and `embed_by_username` is blank/nil, `downcase` will raise `NoMethodError` on `nil`. There is no guard for `embed_by_username` in `TopicRetriever` (unlike `Jobs::PollFeed.execute`, which checks it), and `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable` also doesn’t enforce it, so the crash is reachable.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Jobs::PollFeed is invoked synchronously via Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({}) from the request-triggered retriever path, causing the entire feed to be downloaded and imported inline on the embed request path (lib/topic_retriever.rb:40)

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#best`, when no topic is found it enqueues `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)` and immediately renders `loading`; it does not run retrieval inline in the HTTP request. The synchronous call `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` exists in `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve`, but `TopicRetriever` is invoked from the background `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` job (`app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb`), not directly on the request thread. So the finding’s claim that the feed is downloaded/imported “inline on the embed request path” is not verifiable from this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: PollFeed and the retriever re-evaluate guard conditions inconsistently (PollFeed checks feed_polling_url/embed_by_username, the retriever doesn't), and the two entry points can race on TopicEmbed.import

adjudication.rationale:
The race concern is real: TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve does a non-atomic check `return if TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: @embed_url).exists?` and then may later call either `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` (which can create TopicEmbeds) and/or `fetch_http` -> `TopicEmbed.import_remote` -> `TopicEmbed.import`. In `TopicEmbed.import`, creation is `embed = TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` followed by `TopicEmbed.create!` inside a transaction, but there is no locking; two concurrent callers (e.g., scheduled PollFeed and an on-demand RetrieveTopic job for the same URL) can both see no row and attempt to create, causing a unique-index violation on `topic_embeds.embed_url` and potentially leaving an extra Topic/Post created before the failing `create!`. 

The “inconsistent guard conditions” part is weaker: TopicRetriever doesn’t check `feed_polling_url`/`embed_by_username` before calling PollFeed, but PollFeed.execute itself guards on those, so it won’t poll. However, TopicRetriever#fetch_http does call `SiteSetting.embed_by_username.downcase` without a presence check, which can raise if unset—this is a real inconsistency/bug, but it’s not exactly as stated in the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Weak origin check in embed.js uses substring matching (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1) instead of exact origin comparison, allowing spoofed origins like http://forum.example.com.attacker.tld to pass and inject e.data.height into the iframe style
matched_golden_ids: The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both comments flag the same security issue: origin validation relies on indexOf/substring matching rather than exact origin comparison, allowing crafted malicious domains (e.g., evil-discourseUrl.com or forum.example.com.attacker.tld) to bypass the check.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unescaped URL interpolated into single-quoted HTML attribute in the imported-from footer (app/models/topic_embed.rb:14), allowing attribute breakout since URL is only validated by /^https?::////

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the code appends HTML containing `#{url}` into `contents` (which later becomes `post.raw` and is rendered via `raw post.cooked` in `app/views/embed/best.html.erb`). The only validation on `url` is `return unless url =~ /^https?\:\/\//`, which does not prevent single quotes or other characters that can break out of the single-quoted `href` attribute (e.g., `http://host/' onmouseover='...`). Therefore an attacker-controlled embed/feed URL could inject arbitrary attributes/HTML leading to XSS.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Kernel#open used on setting- and user-influenced URLs (poll_feed.rb:34, topic_embed.rb:52), which is pipe-command susceptible and lacks redirect/size/timeout controls
matched_golden_ids: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The golden issue is SSRF: PollFeed calls `open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` without validating the URL, letting someone who can control that setting make the server fetch arbitrary URLs. The candidate flags `Kernel#open` on setting-/user-influenced URLs in `poll_feed.rb`, which inherently covers the same unvalidated remote fetch risk (SSRF), though it also adds extra concerns (pipe-command susceptibility, missing limits/timeouts).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Check-then-create race on topic_embeds.embed_url unique index in TopicEmbed.import (topic_embed.rb:19-31): concurrent workers race and the loser raises on the unique index with no rescue, and PollFeed sets retry: false so the failure is silent

adjudication.rationale: In TopicEmbed.import, the code does a non-atomic check-then-create: `embed = TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` and, if blank, later `TopicEmbed.create!(..., embed_url: url, ...)` inside a transaction. The migration adds a UNIQUE index on `topic_embeds.embed_url`, so concurrent workers importing the same URL can both observe `embed.blank?` and then race on `create!`, causing the loser to raise an unhandled uniqueness exception (e.g., RecordNotUnique). Jobs::PollFeed sets `sidekiq_options retry: false` and does not rescue around `TopicEmbed.import`, so such a race would cause the job run to fail without being retried, potentially skipping feed imports for that run.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Modified already-shipped migration 20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb adds force: true, which drops and recreates the top_topics table in environments where the migration hasn't run, silently discarding data
topic_embeds migration 20131217174004 has force: true added, a re-run foot-gun

adjudication.rationale: The migration `20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb` is a new file in this diff and defines `create_table :topic_embeds, force: true`. While `force: true` would drop an existing table if the migration were somehow executed when the table already exists, Rails migrations are versioned and normally run only once; re-running the same migration isn’t part of the normal workflow. This is therefore not a clear, verifiable defect introduced by the diff, and the finding’s “added” framing is also inaccurate since there is no prior version shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Editing historical migrations is a maintainability hazard, including whitespace-only churn in migrate_word_counts.rb unrelated to this PR

adjudication.rationale: The diff does edit existing (historical) migrations: `20131210181901_migrate_word_counts.rb` has only whitespace/newline changes, and `20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb` changes `create_table` to add `force: true`. However, the whitespace-only churn is not a functional defect, and “editing historical migrations is a maintainability hazard” is a general process concern rather than a concrete bug/security/correctness issue verifiable from this diff (migrations are normally run once and tracked, so these edits typically have no effect on already-migrated environments).

adjudication_records.issue_text: String#scrub in poll_feed.rb:38 requires Ruby 2.1+, an implicit runtime constraint not declared anywhere
i.content is nil for Atom entries without a <content> element, causing NoMethodError that kills the whole poll run with retry: false (poll_feed.rb:38)

adjudication.rationale: In app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb, the code unconditionally does `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` for each `rss.items` entry. If `i.content` is nil (which is common for feeds/entries that only provide `description`, `summary`, etc.), this will raise `NoMethodError` on `.scrub` and abort the entire poll run. This is a concrete correctness bug in the diff, and it’s exacerbated by `sidekiq_options retry: false`, meaning a transient bad entry can prevent future successful polling unless manually intervened.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Dead code: unused feed_key in poll_feed.rb:19-21, defined but never referenced, suggesting unimplemented Last-Modified/conditional polling

adjudication.rationale: In the new `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, a `feed_key` method is defined (lines 19–21 in that file) and there is no call to `feed_key` anywhere within the diff (neither inside `PollFeed#poll_feed` nor from `TopicRetriever`). However, labeling it as “dead code” is not a verifiable defect from the diff alone: Ruby methods can be invoked externally (e.g., by other parts of the app, scheduled job infrastructure, or future usage), and the proposed implication about unimplemented conditional polling is speculative. At most, it’s an unused-method/code-smell within this diff, not a clear bug/correctness issue proven by the changes shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: God-method TopicEmbed.import (topic_embed.rb:8-33) does five jobs (URL validation, footer injection, hashing, topic/post creation, revision) — service-layer logic living on an AR model with hidden side effects including in-place mutation of the caller's contents string

adjudication.rationale: TopicEmbed.import does append to `contents` via `contents << ...`, so it does mutate the passed-in String in place. However, the proposed finding is primarily an architectural/style critique (“god-method”, “service-layer logic on an AR model”) rather than a clear defect, and the diff does not show any concrete incorrect behavior resulting from that mutation (callers in the diff don’t reuse `contents` afterward). As written, this is not a verifiable bug/security/correctness problem introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Dead require_dependency 'email/sender' in app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb, copy-pasted from a mail job with nothing in this job sending email

adjudication.rationale: In app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb the line `require_dependency 'email/sender'` is not referenced anywhere in the shown job implementation (it only looks up a user and calls `TopicRetriever.new(...).retrieve`). However, an unused `require_dependency` is not, by itself, a clear functional defect introduced by this diff—it’s typically just an unnecessary load. The claim that it’s “copy-pasted from a mail job” is also not verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Duplicated embed-user lookup (User.where(username_lower: SiteSetting.embed_by_username.downcase).first) in poll_feed.rb:27 and topic_retriever.rb:47 with divergent nil-guarding

adjudication.rationale: This is a real issue: both `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` and `TopicRetriever#fetch_http` do `User.where(username_lower: SiteSetting.embed_by_username.downcase).first`, but only `PollFeed#execute` guards that `SiteSetting.embed_by_username.present?` before calling `poll_feed`. In `TopicRetriever`, `fetch_http` can be reached without any prior `embed_by_username` presence check (e.g., via `EmbedController` -> enqueue `:retrieve_topic` -> `TopicRetriever#retrieve` -> `perform_retrieve` -> `fetch_http`), so if `SiteSetting.embed_by_username` is nil/blank, `.downcase` will raise `NoMethodError`. The duplicated code with different surrounding guards makes this divergence likely and verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Leaky indirect contract: RetrieveTopic job receives user_id solely to re-fetch the user and test staff? for the throttle flag (embed_controller.rb:13, retrieve_topic.rb:16-18); throttle policy should be decided at enqueue time

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `EmbedController#best` enqueues `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` with `user_id: current_user.try(:id)` and the job re-fetches the user to compute `no_throttle: user.try(:staff?)` when calling `TopicRetriever`. This is a standard/background-job pattern (jobs can’t carry full user objects) and computing staff status at execution time is reasonable (it even reflects current staff status). The finding is an architectural preference, not a verifiable bug/security/correctness defect introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: current_user will essentially always be nil for embeds rendered in a cross-origin iframe, making the no_throttle staff path in RetrieveTopic effectively unreachable dead logic

adjudication.rationale: In EmbedController#best the job is enqueued with `user_id: current_user.try(:id)`, so `user_id` can indeed be nil when the embed request is unauthenticated. However, the finding claims `current_user` will "essentially always" be nil in a cross-origin iframe, making the staff no-throttle path dead. That is not verifiable from the diff: an iframe request to the Discourse origin can still carry the Discourse session cookie (i.e., `current_user` can be set) unless third‑party cookies are blocked, which is browser/config-dependent and not established by the code here. Additionally, the job could be enqueued from other contexts with a `user_id`. Therefore the "unreachable dead logic" conclusion is speculative rather than a concrete defect shown by this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unused locale key embed.permalink defined in config/locales/server.en.yml but never referenced by any view

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `embed.permalink` under `config/locales/server.en.yml`, and none of the newly added embed views/controllers/models reference `t('embed.permalink')`. However, the claim that it is "never referenced by any view" across the whole codebase is not verifiable from this diff alone (it could be used in existing files not shown), and in any case an extra/unused locale string is not a functional defect introduced by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `force: true` on `create_table :topic_embeds` will silently drop an existing topic_embeds table before recreating it, destroying embed→topic mappings and content_sha1 bookkeeping with no rollback or warning

adjudication.rationale: The new migration `20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb` uses `create_table :topic_embeds, force: true`. In Rails, `force: true` will drop the table first if it already exists and then recreate it. If this migration is accidentally re-run in an environment where `topic_embeds` already exists (e.g., a partially applied/failed migration, manual table creation, or schema load discrepancies), it would silently destroy existing embed→topic mappings and `content_sha1` data before recreating the table. That destructive behavior is introduced by this diff and is not guarded against in the migration.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `force: true` added to already-committed migration CreateTopTopics is destructive DDL that drops the top_topics table and all its aggregated ranking data if the migration re-runs while the table exists

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes an existing migration `CreateTopTopics` from `create_table :top_topics do |t|` to `create_table :top_topics, force: true do |t|`. In Rails, `force: true` causes the table to be dropped before being created if it already exists. This is destructive DDL and would delete any existing `top_topics` data if this migration were ever re-run (e.g., via migrate:redo/rollback+up, or other workflows that execute the migration against a DB that already has the table). Previously it would error instead of dropping data.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Editing the already-shipped migration CreateTopTopics violates migration immutability, causing environments that applied version 20131223171005 to diverge in behavior and making db:schema:load vs db:migrate paths inconsistent

Raw HTML import path (Post.rb cook_method raw_html combined with embed/best.html.erb rendering raw post.cooked) bypasses the sanitizer and after_post_cook filters, resulting in stored XSS on the Discourse origin for embed visitors

adjudication.rationale: Yes. The diff adds a `cook_method` path where `Post#cook` returns `raw` directly when `cook_method == :raw_html`, explicitly skipping the normal cooking pipeline (`post_analyzer.cook`) and the `:after_post_cook` filter. `TopicEmbed.import` creates posts with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and `skip_validations: true`, and the RSS polling job passes untrusted feed content (`CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`) into `TopicEmbed.import` without any sanitization. The embed UI then renders it with `<%= raw post.cooked %>` in `app/views/embed/best.html.erb`. Because in this mode `cooked` effectively equals unsanitized `raw`, malicious HTML/JS from a feed (e.g., `<script>` or dangerous attributes) can be stored and served from the Discourse origin to embed visitors (and potentially elsewhere Discourse renders `cooked` as trusted).

adjudication_records.issue_text: topic_embeds lacks index/FK on topic_id and post_id, so deleted topics leave orphaned embed rows that cause EmbedController#best to raise on a missing topic instead of gracefully falling back

adjudication.rationale: In the new migration `CreateTopicEmbeds`, the table has `topic_id` and `post_id` columns but only adds a unique index on `embed_url`; there are no foreign keys and no indexes on `topic_id`/`post_id`. Nothing in the diff adds `dependent: :destroy` from `Topic`/`Post` back to `TopicEmbed` either. That means if a topic/post is deleted, an orphaned `topic_embeds` row can remain. `EmbedController#best` uses `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` (a blind `pluck(:topic_id).first`) and then instantiates `TopicView.new(topic_id, ...)` without checking that the topic still exists, so an orphaned row can lead to an exception / error response rather than falling back to the enqueue+loading path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: embed_url is stored and compared without normalization, so scheme/trailing-slash variants create duplicate topics for the same article and cause lookups to miss existing embeds and re-enqueue retrieval forever

adjudication.rationale: Yes: the diff stores and queries `embed_url` using exact string equality with no canonicalization. `TopicEmbed.import` persists `embed_url: url` as provided, and lookups use `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: embed_url)` / `topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` with a unique index on the raw string only. This means variants like `http` vs `https`, trailing slash differences, query-string ordering, or redirected/canonical URLs will be treated as different records, leading to duplicate topics and missed lookups for an already-imported article when a different variant is requested. The claim that it will "re-enqueue retrieval forever" is somewhat overstated (it will keep enqueueing for that variant until it creates a record for that exact string), but the underlying duplicate/missed-lookup problem is real and verifiable in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: cook_method column default of 1 hardcodes the magic Enum position of Post.cook_methods[:regular] in the schema, so reordering the enum would silently change the meaning of existing rows

adjudication.rationale: The migration `AddCookMethodToPosts` adds `cook_method` as an integer with `default: 1`. In the same diff, `Post.cook_methods` is defined as `Enum.new(:regular, :raw_html)`, so the meaning of `1` is tied to the enum’s positional mapping (i.e., whatever `Enum` assigns to the first element). Because the DB stores the integer and the default is a literal, any future reordering/insertion in `Enum.new(...)` would change what existing rows (and the default) mean without any DB change or explicit remapping. This brittleness is directly present in the diff (hardcoded default + position-based enum).

adjudication_records.issue_text: The raw_html cook method in post.rb:131 bypasses the entire cooking/sanitization pipeline with no downstream sanitization

adjudication.rationale: Yes. The diff introduces `Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and in `Post#cook` immediately `return raw` when that cook_method is set, skipping the normal cooking pipeline (which is where Discourse typically sanitizes/filters HTML). `TopicEmbed.import` and `Jobs::PollFeed` create/update posts with `cook_method: :raw_html` using untrusted remote content (`SimpleRSS.parse(open(...))` content and `Readability::Document` content) and there is no other sanitization step shown before rendering (`embed/best.html.erb` does `<%= raw post.cooked %>`). This creates a verifiable XSS risk via embedded/imported HTML.

adjudication_records.issue_text: PollFeed passes unescaped feed content (i.content) straight to TopicEmbed.import with no tag/attribute whitelist, allowing script, iframe, onerror handlers, or javascript: hrefs to be stored and rendered verbatim

adjudication.rationale: In `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed`, feed item content is taken from `i.content`, HTML-unescaped via `CGI.unescapeHTML`, and passed directly to `TopicEmbed.import`. `TopicEmbed.import` then creates a post with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, and `Post#cook` returns `raw` verbatim for `:raw_html`, bypassing the normal rendering/sanitization pipeline. As a result, any scripts/iframes/event handlers or `javascript:` URLs present in feed content can be stored and later rendered directly (e.g., the embed view uses `<%= raw post.cooked %>`), which is a verifiable XSS risk introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: embed/best.html.erb renders post.cooked with raw output, so stored malicious HTML from feeds is rendered unsanitized

adjudication.rationale:
Yes. The new embed view explicitly outputs HTML without escaping: `
<%= raw post.cooked %>
` in `app/views/embed/best.html.erb`. The diff also introduces a `:raw_html` cook method in `Post#cook` that returns `raw` directly, bypassing the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline. Feed-imported content comes from external sources (e.g., `Jobs::PollFeed` uses `SimpleRSS.parse` and then `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`), and `TopicEmbed.import` stores it as the post `raw` with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`. There is no sanitization step shown for this RSS content, so malicious HTML (including `

adjudication_records.issue_text: The readability path (import_remote) whitelists a[href] but does not sanitize URL schemes, so javascript: hrefs survive; absolutize_urls only rewrites hrefs starting with / and does not sanitize schemes

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `TopicEmbed.import_remote`, the code uses `Readability::Document.new(..., tags: [..., 'a', 'img'], attributes: %w[href src])` and then passes `doc.content` into `TopicEmbed.import`. `TopicEmbed.import` stores/render this as `raw_html` (via `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`), and `Post#cook` returns `raw` directly for `raw_html`, bypassing the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline. The only transformation applied is `absolutize_urls`, which rewrites only `href/src` values starting with `/` and does not sanitize or restrict URL schemes. Therefore `href="javascript:..."` (and other dangerous schemes) would remain in the stored/rendered HTML.

adjudication_records.issue_text: /embed/best is served from the forum's own origin with X-Frame-Options set to ALLOWALL, so injected scripts execute with full access on the forum origin
